vibe: Patch the edge and management plane first: Cisco mail gateways, VMware vCenter and a browser-to-Windows zero-day chain are all active, while AI labs edge toward rare safety coordination.

cyber.title: Cisco patches Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks
cyber.summary: Cisco patched CVE-2026-76461, an unauthenticated Secure Email Gateway flaw already exploited to execute commands as root. Internet-facing appliances deserve immediate patching and compromise review.

cyber.title: CISA: Critical VMware RCE flaw now exploited by ransomware gangs
cyber.summary: CISA says ransomware crews are now exploiting a critical VMware vCenter remote-code-execution flaw. Patch exposed management planes immediately and hunt for post-exploitation activity.

cyber.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit Chrome-Windows Zero-Day Chain to Deploy GRIMWEDGE
cyber.summary: A China-linked campaign chained Chrome and Windows zero-days to deploy GRIMWEDGE. Update browsers and Windows promptly; the chain shows why endpoint patch lag is especially dangerous.

cyber.title: Human Attacker Exploits Marimo RCE, Reaches SSH Bastion in Eight Seconds
cyber.summary: A disclosed Marimo remote-code-execution path let a human attacker reach an SSH bastion in eight seconds, underscoring the risk of exposed developer tools and inherited cloud credentials.

cyber.title: Mass-Scanning Campaign Exploits Vite Flaw to Extract Cloud Credentials From Exposed Dev Servers
cyber.summary: Mass scanning is targeting exposed Vite development servers to extract AWS and Azure credentials. Keep dev servers private and rotate secrets from any reachable instance.

cyber.title: September Patch Tuesday: two exploited zero-days among 972 CVEs
cyber.summary: CrowdStrike's September review counts two exploited zero-days and 113 critical vulnerabilities among 972 CVEs, with Windows Kerberos, SQL Server and Office prominent in the urgent set.

cyber.title: America's Driver's License Breach Is a National Security Disaster
cyber.summary: A widely discussed analysis argues the US driver-licence breach is infrastructure-scale identity exposure, with long-lived consequences for fraud and identity verification.

cyber.title: BambooToken malware controls Windows and Linux systems via MQTT
cyber.summary: BambooToken uses MQTT as command-and-control across Windows and Linux, a useful detection case for defenders monitoring unusual broker traffic.

cyber.title: Hackers target WordPress sites via third-party WooCommerce plugin
cyber.summary: Attackers are abusing a third-party WooCommerce plugin to compromise WordPress sites. Operators should inventory plugins, update promptly and review admin accounts.

cyber.title: Electric and gas utility CenterPoint Energy warns of data breach after dark web post
cyber.summary: CenterPoint Energy acknowledged a breach after data appeared on a dark-web forum, adding another critical-infrastructure exposure to the week.

ai.title: Agent-net Open Sources Webagent: A Go Harness That Turns Any Website into a Guarded AI Agent
ai.summary: Agent-net released Webagent, a Go harness that wraps websites as guarded AI agents with an emphasis on permissions and control boundaries.

ai.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google have been in talks on AI safety for weeks
ai.summary: The three frontier labs have been coordinating on AI-safety measures for weeks, turning the slowdown debate into a concrete cross-company effort.

ai.title: Early Anthropic hire, former METR COO have found a way to rein in rogue AI agents
ai.summary: A new effort from former Anthropic and METR leaders targets rogue-agent containment, directly relevant to permissioning, monitoring and agent governance.

ai.title: A single firm is behind OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta hacking scandals
ai.summary: An investigation ties one firm to several recent AI-lab hacking controversies, raising uncomfortable questions about outsourced security research and disclosure incentives.

ai.title: AI models need more data about biology, and OpenAI is paying to create it
ai.summary: OpenAI is funding the creation of new biological datasets, a sign that frontier-model progress is increasingly constrained by scarce, specialised training data.

ai.title: Hugging Face is billing OpenAI $100M for hacking it
ai.summary: Hugging Face is reportedly demanding $100 million over compute traces linked to the recent intrusion, escalating the dispute from disclosure into a major commercial claim.

ai.title: OpenAI buys smartphone camera maker Glass Imaging for $300M
ai.summary: OpenAI reportedly bought computational-photography company Glass Imaging for $300 million, extending its push into cameras, devices and multimodal capture.

ai.title: Open weights are not open source: Why AI's favorite label is under dispute
ai.summary: A useful explainer separates downloadable model weights from genuinely open-source AI, where data, training code and reproducibility remain contested.

it.title: iOS 27 is finally here, with the new Siri AI beta – and 120 security patches
it.summary: iOS 27 ships the new Siri AI beta alongside roughly 120 security fixes. The patch volume alone makes this a worthwhile early update.

it.title: September's Windows 11 patch needs an emergency patch of its own
it.summary: Microsoft issued an emergency correction for September's Windows 11 update. Administrators should verify the follow-up patch before broad deployment.

it.title: PostgreSQL 19 graph queries fail the 'would you ship this?' test
it.summary: Early PostgreSQL 19 graph-query behaviour is drawing criticism over production readiness; useful context for database teams evaluating the feature.

videos.title: Anthropic researchers are quitting... and now we know why
videos.verdict: SKIM — a sharp eight-minute summary; use it as an entry point, then read primary sources.
videos.summary: Fireship recaps the viral resignation of Anthropic researcher Jacob Hilton and the widening call to slow frontier AI, with context on recursive self-improvement and lab incentives.

videos.title: Claude Is Now Leaving Invisible Fingerprints In Its Text
videos.verdict: WATCH — concise and unusually practical for anyone publishing AI-assisted text.
videos.summary: Two Minute Papers explains Anthropic's statistical text fingerprinting: invisible token-choice patterns designed to identify Claude-generated text without hidden characters.

videos.title: How Hackers Steal Your Accounts Even With 2FA Enabled
videos.verdict: SKIM — the account-theft and session-cookie sections carry the value.
videos.summary: A long, practical discussion of modern account theft: infostealers, adversary-in-the-middle phishing, session-cookie replay and why MFA alone is not a complete defence.

videos.title: What Is Legacy Code? How AI Is Modernizing Legacy Systems
videos.verdict: SKIM — a clear overview rather than deep implementation guidance.
videos.summary: IBM explains why legacy-code modernisation is risky and where AI can help with understanding, testing and incremental migration without pretending it removes review.

videos.title: you can't be serious
videos.verdict: SKIM — watch the opening Steam privilege-escalation analysis.
videos.summary: John Hammond examines a Windows Steam local privilege-escalation proof of concept and discusses the uncertainty and verification work around fresh vulnerability claims.

videos.title: Claude Skills Explained: Unslop
videos.verdict: SKIM — useful if you build Claude or ChatGPT skills.
videos.summary: A short demo of the Unslop skill, which audits recurring AI-writing patterns and rewrites for more human rhythm and specificity.
